claims.text: The initial refractory high-entropy alloy exhibits significant weight gain during high-temperature oxygen exposure.
Adding aluminum to the refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Aluminum addition will promote in situ formation of a continuous Al2O3 scale.
The intervention may be implemented by melt addition or surface alloying.
The proposed protection should operate at approximately 1100–1200 °C in air or another oxygen-rich atmosphere for at least about 24 hours.
Aluminum addition produces a dense, adherent Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale impedes oxygen diffusion to the underlying alloy.
Added aluminum preferentially oxidizes during high-temperature exposure.
The resulting Al2O3 layer is stable and slow-growing under the proposed exposure conditions.
Limiting oxygen transport through the Al2O3 layer minimizes further oxidation of the substrate.
Relative to the untreated alloy, the aluminum-enhanced alloy will have a substantially lower oxidation rate and reduced weight gain.
Relative to the untreated alloy, the aluminum-enhanced alloy will retain better surface integrity after exposure.
The untreated alloy has higher weight gain and more extensive oxide-scale formation because it lacks a protective alumina layer.
Protection depends on optimizing the aluminum concentration sufficiently to form a continuous alumina scale.
Excess or otherwise nonoptimized aluminum may adversely affect the alloy's intrinsic mechanical properties.
Protection requires an operating environment in which Al2O3 can form and remain stable.
Improvement magnitude and cyclic lifetime may vary because of interactions among alloying elements and scale-formation kinetics.
Baseline and aluminum-treated samples will be compared after identical 1100–1200 °C oxygen-rich exposures lasting 24 hours.
Weight gain, oxide phases, and oxide-scale microstructure will be measured using gravimetry, SEM/EDS, and XRD.
The hypothesis is falsified if aluminum addition neither significantly reduces weight gain nor produces a continuous protective Al2O3 layer relative to the untreated control.
